fact-check: to check that the facts in a claim or article are true
fall in love: to begin to love someone deeply
fall into place: for the parts of a plan to start working out clearly
feature story: a long article in a newspaper about one subject
figure out: to understand something, or to find a way to do it
final exam: the last and usually biggest test at the end of a course
finish / complete / conclude: to bring something to its end, or to end formally
fire brigade: the team trained and equipped to put out fires
fire extinguisher: a small container of foam or gas for putting out a fire
fire station: the building where firefighters and their engines are based
fire truck: the large vehicle firefighters drive to a fire
first aid: simple medical help given before a doctor arrives
fitting room: a small room in a shop where you try clothes on
fold the laundry: to fold clean clothes neatly after washing
follow up: to check on something later, or to act on it further
forbid / prohibit / ban: to order that something must not be done
fossil fuels: coal, oil and gas formed underground over millions of years
get along: to have a friendly relationship with someone
get along with: to have a friendly relationship with someone
get away: to escape, or to take a holiday
get better: to improve, or to recover from an illness
get cold feet: to become nervous and want to avoid something you agreed to do
get down to brass tacks: to start dealing with the practical details
get up: to rise from bed or from a seat
get used to: to become familiar with something and stop finding it strange
give advice: to tell someone what you think they should do
give an opinion: to say what you think about something
give away: to give something for free, or to reveal a secret by accident
give in: to stop resisting and accept what you were fighting against
give it a shot: to try something, even if you are not sure you will succeed
give the benefit of the doubt: to believe someone is telling the truth when you cannot be sure
give up: to stop trying, or to stop a habit
global warming: the rise in the earth's temperature caused by greenhouse gases
go down in history: to be remembered for a long time for something important
go over: to examine or repeat something carefully
go the extra mile: to do more than you were asked in order to help
go through: to experience something difficult, or to search inside something
go to bed: to get into bed to sleep
go to great lengths: to try very hard, using every means
go to work: to travel to your job and start working
golden opportunity: a rare chance that is worth taking
gpa: the average of your grades, used by American schools
green bean: a long thin green pod eaten as a vegetable
greenhouse gas: a gas such as carbon dioxide that traps heat in the air
hammer it home: to repeat something until it is fully understood
hang out: to spend time relaxing with people
hang out the washing: to put washed clothes on a line to dry
hang up: to end a phone call, or to put something on a hook
happy / glad / delighted: feeling pleasure, from quiet satisfaction to great joy
hard drive: the part of a computer that stores all its files
hashtag: a word with the # sign that groups posts on social media
have breakfast: to eat the first meal of the day
have dinner: to eat the main evening meal
hear / listen / heed: to receive sound, to pay attention to it, or to act on advice
heatwave: a long period of unusually hot weather
heavy rain: rain falling hard and in large amounts
heavy traffic: many vehicles moving slowly on the roads
hide / conceal / mask: to keep something from being seen or known
hit the nail on the head: to say exactly the right thing about a situation
hold a meeting: to arrange and run a meeting
hold an opinion: to have a particular view about something
how: in what way; used to ask about the manner of something
